# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)

term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/ reached the disk or the
# folder's .git. Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

fail=0
for p in vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"

# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/ reached the disk or the
# folder's .git. Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

fail=0
for p in vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

"""Archives a finished session's transcript into sessions/ (R-CLEAN-3).

  archive-session.py TRANSCRIPT.jsonl --role clean|spec [--out sessions/<role>]

clean session archives only clean sessions; a spec session may archive
either (sessions/README.md). It copies the transcript to
`sessions/<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` (the date is
the UTC date of its first entry), along with any subagent transcripts
(`<id>/subagents/*.jsonl` next to it) into `<same name>.subagents/`. It
redacts:
  - tokens and keys (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, bearer tokens, private keys);
  - e-mail addresses, except no-reply addresses;
  - account and organisation IDs;
  - private paths: home folders become `~`, and per-user temp folders are
    shortened;
  - the local user names seen in those paths and the user running this,
    wherever they appear (ignoring case, even inside other words), and
    `*.local` host names;
  - the local top-level folder (the folder that holds this checkout, unless
    that is just the repository's own name; or --top NAME), anywhere, as
    `<top>`;
  - the owner's private terms (PRIVATE_TERMS, or the gitignored
    tools/[REDACTED:host]; tools/check-private.py), anywhere;
  - in clean transcripts only: the lines of a git summary (a merge's
    diffstat, `create mode` and `delete mode` lines) that name files under
    vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/. Each run of such lines
    becomes one note saying how many were removed. A name shortened to
    `.../tail` counts when its tail matches only such files.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Checks archived session transcripts (R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3, R-CLEAN-5;
check C-TRANSCRIPTS).

  check-transcripts.py [SESSIONS_DIR]        (default: sessions/)

Each archived session is `<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` under
SESSIONS_DIR (role clean or spec, and the folder must match the name), with
its redaction note `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside it, and any subagent
transcripts in `<same name>.subagents/*.jsonl`.

Spec-side transcripts (`spec/`) are left out of clean folders. When `spec/`
isn't on disk, they are skipped, never looked for elsewhere, and the output
says so.

For every transcript:
  - the SessionStart banner (tools/session-banner.sh) must be there, with
    `status: OK` and exit code 0. Any CONFIG MISMATCH or failed SessionStart
    hook fails. (EXEMPT_NO_BANNER lists the only sessions allowed to have
    none, and why.)
For every clean-side transcript, including its subagents:
  - every file read, write, search, web fetch, web search and shell command
    is listed, and any that touches FORBIDDEN fails, unless that exact tool
    call is in sessions/REVIEWED.json (a reviewed false positive, such as a
    shell command that only writes a document naming a forbidden folder).
    Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging.

The format is Claude Code's JSONL transcript: tool calls are `tool_use`
blocks inside `type: "assistant"` entries; hook output is an `attachment`
entry with `hookEvent: "SessionStart"`, `stdout` and `exitCode` (PROVENANCE
P-6). Other entries are not inspected for tool use.
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-(clean|spec)-([0-9a-f-]{36})\.jsonl$")
BANNER_START = "=== small-beeps session banner v1 ==="

EXEMPT_NO_BANNER = {
    "36860ab8-77fd-4fd6-aa1d-2063c15a5548":
        "M0a, the first session: it began before tools/session-banner.sh and "
        "its hook existed (docs/EXPOSURE.md, Addendum 2 step 5)",
    "ddebd686-9190-4fa3-b217-30d0a98fda69":
        "a one-prompt `claude -p` run started by M0a in its scratch folder to "
        "learn how hook output is stored; its only hook printed a test marker, "
        "and it made no tool calls (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0a)",
    "e74c69f7-ff95-4dcc-bf7a-9a980e62a6f9":
        "M0b, the first spec-side session: it began under the owner's hand-made "
        "settings, before tools/spec-setup.sh installed the banner hook in its "
        "folder (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0b)",
}
ROLES = ("clean", "spec")

# Mirrors CONTRIBUTING.md, "Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or
# quotes". Each pattern is matched, case-insensitively, against the targets
# of reads, searches, fetches and shell commands (not against the contents
# a session writes).
FORBIDDEN = [
    ("Felucca and firmwares built on it", r"felucca|hortator|ghoulbox|melodee|\bskiff\b"),
    ("hugelton (Felucca's author)", r"hugelton"),
    ("dinghy", r"dinghy|zvenson"),
    ("FM-1 SID firmware", r"fm1-sid"),
    ("emulator probe source", r"probes/lcdtest\.c"),
    ("F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository", r"fm1-emu|f-emulator"),
    ("emulator crates", r"\bcrates/fm1-"),
    # A path into the folder, or the folder itself as a whole word.
    ("vendor/emulator/ (spec side)", r"(^|[\s\"'=:/])vendor/emulator(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("harness/ source (spec side)", r"(^|[\s\"'=:/])harness(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("thefirmwarehub.com", r"thefirmwarehub\.com"),
    ("spec-side session transcripts", r"sessions/spec(/|[\s\"']|$)"),
    ("FM-1-RE firmware images or disassembly",
     r"fm-1-re.*(firmware-images|disasm|disassembl|ghidra|\.idb\b|\.i64\b|functions)"
     r"|firmware-images/"),
    ("M-VAVE stock firmware", r"m-?vave.*\.(fwsc|bin|ufw|hex)\b"),
]
FORBIDDEN_RE = [(why, re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE)) for why, p in FORBIDDEN]


def targets(name, inp):
    """Returns (kind, target) pairs for one tool call."""
    s = lambda k: str(inp.get(k, "")) if inp.get(k) is not None else ""
    if name == "Read":
        return [("read", s("file_path"))]
    if name in ("Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"):
        return [("write", s("file_path") or s("notebook_path"))]
    if name == "Grep":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("glob"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "Glob":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "WebFetch":
        return [("fetch", s("url"))]
    if name == "WebSearch":
        return [("web-search", s("query"))]
    if name == "Bash":
        return [("shell", s("command"))]
    if name in ("Agent", "Task"):
        return [("agent", s("description"))]
    if name.startswith("mcp__"):
        out = []
        for k, v in sorted(inp.items()):
            if isinstance(v, str) and (k in ("url", "path", "file_path", "query")
                                       or v.startswith("http")):
                out.append(("mcp", "%s=%s" % (k, v)))
        return out
    return []


def forbidden_hits(kind, target):
    if kind in ("write", "agent"):
        return []  # what a session writes isn't a read; agents have own transcripts
    return [why for why, rx in FORBIDDEN_RE if rx.search(target)]


def load(path):
    entries = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for n, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            if line.strip():
                try:
                    entries.append(json.loads(line))
                except ValueError as e:
                    raise SystemExit("%s:%d: not JSON (%s)" % (path, n, e))
    return entries


def banners(entries):
    """Yields (exit_code, stdout) for every SessionStart hook run."""
    for e in entries:
        a = e.get("attachment") if e.get("type") == "attachment" else None
        if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("hookEvent") == "SessionStart":
            yield a.get("exitCode"), a.get("stdout") or a.get("content") or "", a.get("stderr") or ""


def tool_calls(entries):
    for e in entries:
        if e.get("type") != "assistant":
            continue
        content = (e.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if not isinstance(content, list):
            continue
        for block in content:
            if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_use":
                yield block.get("id", ""), block.get("name", ""), block.get("input") or {}
    # Files attached to a user message (e.g. @-mentions) are reads too.
    for e in entries:
        a = e.get("attachment") if e.get("type") == "attachment" else None
        if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("type") in ("file", "directory", "opened_file_in_ide",
                                                       "selected_lines_in_ide", "compact_file_reference"):
            yield e.get("uuid", ""), "Read", {"file_path": a.get("filename") or a.get("path") or ""}


def load_reviewed(sessions_dir):
    """sessions/REVIEWED.json: hits that people reviewed and found not to be
    a touch of forbidden material (e.g. a shell command that only *writes*
    a document naming a forbidden folder). Each entry names the session, the
    tool call's ID, the matched rule and the reason. It is added by pull
    request, so the owner's signed merge approves it."""
    path = os.path.join(sessions_dir, "REVIEWED.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path) and os.path.basename(sessions_dir.rstrip("/")) in ROLES:
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(sessions_dir.rstrip("/")), "REVIEWED.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return {}
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    reviewed = {}
    for r in data.get("reviewed", []):
        if not (r.get("session") and r.get("tool_use_id") and r.get("rule") and r.get("reason")):
            raise SystemExit("%s: every entry needs session, tool_use_id, rule and reason" % path)
        reviewed[(r["session"], r["tool_use_id"], r["rule"])] = r["reason"]
    return reviewed


def check_banner(sid, entries, problems):
    runs = list(banners(entries))
    ok = 0
    for code, out, err in runs:
        if "CONFIG MISMATCH" in out or "CONFIG MISMATCH" in err:
            problems.append("CONFIG MISMATCH in SessionStart banner")
        elif BANNER_START in out:
            if code not in (0, None) or "status: OK" not in out:
                problems.append("SessionStart banner without status OK (exit %s)" % code)
            else:
                ok += 1
        elif code not in (0, None):
            problems.append("a SessionStart hook failed (exit %s)" % code)
    if ok:
        return "banner OK (%d)" % ok
    if sid in EXEMPT_NO_BANNER:
        return "no banner, exempt: " + EXEMPT_NO_BANNER[sid]
    problems.append("no SessionStart banner")
    return "no banner"


def check_session(path, reviewed=None):
    reviewed = reviewed if reviewed is not None else load_reviewed(os.path.dirname(path))
    base = os.path.basename(path)
    m = NAME_RE.match(base)
    if not m:
        return ["file name doesn't match <date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl"], []
    date, role, sid = m.groups()
    problems = []
    lines = []
    folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)))
    if folder in ROLES and folder != role:
        problems.append("a %s-side transcript in %s/" % (role, folder))
    if not os.path.exists(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".REDACTIONS.md"):
        problems.append("redaction note %s.REDACTIONS.md is missing" % base[:-6])
    entries = load(path)
    lines.append("%s (%s side, session %s, %s): %s"
                 % (base, role, sid, date, check_banner(sid, entries, problems)))
    if role == "clean":
        files = [path] + sorted(glob.glob(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".subagents/*.jsonl"))
        count = 0
        for f in files:
            sub = "" if f == path else " [subagent %s]" % os.path.basename(f)
            for tid, name, inp in tool_calls(load(f) if f != path else entries):
                for kind, target in targets(name, inp):
                    count += 1
                    hits = forbidden_hits(kind, target)
                    shown = target.replace("\n", "\\n")
                    if len(shown) > 240:
                        shown = shown[:240] + "..."
                    lines.append("  %-10s %-9s %s%s" % (kind, name[:9], shown, sub))
                    for why in hits:
                        reason = reviewed.get((sid, tid, why))
                        if reason:
                            lines.append("    REVIEWED %s (%s): %s" % (tid, why, reason))
                        else:
                            problems.append("%s %s %s touches forbidden material (%s): %s"
                                            % (kind, name, tid, why, shown[:120]))
        lines.append("  %d reads, writes, searches, fetches and commands listed" % count)
    return problems, lines


def main():
    root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    sessions = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(root, "sessions")
    reviewed = load_reviewed(sessions)
    failed = False
    # anywhere else under sessions/ (an auditor's transcript, say: those are never archived here)
    for stray in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sessions, "**", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True)):
        rel = os.path.relpath(stray, sessions).replace(os.sep, "/")
        if rel.split("/")[0] not in ROLES:
            print("FAIL %s: a transcript outside clean/ and spec/" % rel)
            failed = True
    paths = []
    for role in ROLES:
        d = os.path.join(sessions, role)
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            print("%s/: not on disk; %s-side transcripts skipped, not read%s"
                  % (role, role, " (a clean folder leaves them out)" if role == "spec" else ""))
            continue
        paths += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.jsonl")))
    for p in paths:
        problems, lines = check_session(p, reviewed)
        for l in lines:
            print(l)
        for pr in problems:
            print("FAIL %s: %s" % (os.path.basename(p), pr))
        failed = failed or bool(problems)
    print("%d archived transcript(s) checked: %s"
          % (len(paths), "FAIL" if failed else "PASS"))
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(sessions_dir.rstrip("/")), "REVIEWED.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return {}
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    reviewed = {}
    for r in data.get("reviewed", []):
        if not (r.get("session") and r.get("tool_use_id") and r.get("rule") and r.get("reason")):
            raise SystemExit("%s: every entry needs session, tool_use_id, rule and reason" % path)
        reviewed[(r["session"], r["tool_use_id"], r["rule"])] = r["reason"]
    return reviewed


def check_banner(sid, entries, problems):
    runs = list(banners(entries))
    ok = 0
    for code, out, err in runs:
        if "CONFIG MISMATCH" in out or "CONFIG MISMATCH" in err:
            problems.append("CONFIG MISMATCH in SessionStart banner")
        elif BANNER_START in out:
            if code not in (0, None) or "status: OK" not in out:
                problems.append("SessionStart banner without status OK (exit %s)" % code)
            else:
                ok += 1
        elif code not in (0, None):
            problems.append("a SessionStart hook failed (exit %s)" % code)
    if ok:
        return "banner OK (%d)" % ok
    if sid in EXEMPT_NO_BANNER:
        return "no banner, exempt: " + EXEMPT_NO_BANNER[sid]
    problems.append("no SessionStart banner")
    return "no banner"


def check_session(path, reviewed=None):
    reviewed = reviewed if reviewed is not None else load_reviewed(os.path.dirname(path))
    base = os.path.basename(path)
    m = NAME_RE.match(base)
    if not m:
        return ["file name doesn't match <date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl"], []
    date, role, sid = m.groups()
    problems = []
    lines = []
    folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)))
    if folder in ROLES and folder != role:
        problems.append("a %s-side transcript in %s/" % (role, folder))
    if not os.path.exists(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".REDACTIONS.md"):
        problems.append("redaction note %s.REDACTIONS.md is missing" % base[:-6])
    entries = load(path)
    lines.append("%s (%s side, session %s, %s): %s"
                 % (base, role, sid, date, check_banner(sid, entries, problems)))
    if role == "clean":
        files = [path] + sorted(glob.glob(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".subagents/*.jsonl"))
        count = 0
        for f in files:
            sub = "" if f == path else " [subagent %s]" % os.path.basename(f)
            for tid, name, inp in tool_calls(load(f) if f != path else entries):
                for kind, target in targets(name, inp):
                    count += 1
                    hits = forbidden_hits(kind, target)
                    shown = target.replace("\n", "\\n")
                    if len(shown) > 240:
                        shown = shown[:240] + "..."
                    lines.append("  %-10s %-9s %s%s" % (kind, name[:9], shown, sub))
                    for why in hits:
                        reason = reviewed.get((sid, tid, why))
                        if reason:
                            lines.append("    REVIEWED %s (%s): %s" % (tid, why, reason))
                        else:
                            problems.append("%s %s %s touches forbidden material (%s): %s"
                                            % (kind, name, tid, why, shown[:120]))
        lines.append("  %d reads, writes, searches, fetches and commands listed" % count)
    return problems, lines


def main():
    root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    sessions = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(root, "sessions")
    reviewed = load_reviewed(sessions)
    failed = False
    # anywhere else under sessions/ (an auditor's transcript, say: those are never archived here)
    for stray in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sessions, "**", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True)):
        rel = os.path.relpath(stray, sessions).replace(os.sep, "/")
        if rel.split("/")[0] not in ROLES:
            print("FAIL %s: a transcript outside clean/ and spec/" % rel)
            failed = True
    paths = []
    for role in ROLES:
        d = os.path.join(sessions, role)
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            print("%s/: not on disk; %s-side transcripts skipped, not read%s"
                  % (role, role, " (a clean folder leaves them out)" if role == "spec" else ""))
            continue
        paths += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "*.jsonl")))
    for p in paths:
        problems, lines = check_session(p, reviewed)
        for l in lines:
            print(l)
        for pr in problems:
            print("FAIL %s: %s" % (os.path.basename(p), pr))
        failed = failed or bool(problems)
    print("%d archived transcript(s) checked: %s"
          % (len(paths), "FAIL" if failed else "PASS"))
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# M1: boot (clocks, interrupts, timer)

## 0. Start safely, and close M0

1. Check the banner says status OK; if not, stop and tell the owner.
2. Run tools/clean-update.sh. It must end with "no spec-side files on disk or in .git"; if anything prints STOP, stop and tell the owner.
3. Check that tools/[REDACTED:host] exists (don't open it).
4. Archive the clean sessions not yet in sessions/clean/ and run tools/check-transcripts.py. Never open anything under sessions/spec/.
5. Add your entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md. Save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/M1.md in your first commit.
6. If the owner has pushed the signed tag `m0`, create the M0 GitHub release from it (gh release create m0 --verify-tag): the firmware image and ELF built from that commit, its record, and an SBOM; generic release notes while the repo is low profile. If the tag isn't there yet, skip this and remind the owner at the end.

## 1. Scope

Bring the chip from reset to a known, timed, interrupt-driven state, using only what docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md, the vendored SDK headers and the allowed FM-1-RE documents say:
- **Clocks:** set the system clocks the firmware will run at, as the spec allows, and verify them by black-box measurement in fwtest.
- **Interrupts:** our own vector table and handler entry/exit, with nesting and priorities only as far as M1 needs; a fault or unexpected interrupt is reported over the debug channel and halts cleanly, so tests can detect it.
- **Timer:** a periodic timer interrupt as the system tick. The heartbeat moves from polling to the tick, and the main loop idles in the low-power wait between ticks.
- **Core 1:** only if the spec makes it necessary for M1; otherwise leave it parked and say so in the design notes.

Where the spec gives requirements, meet them with your own design. Where it is silent or a fact is emulator-only, either confirm it with your own black-box test or file a spec request in docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md (by PR) and tell the owner. Never look anywhere else.

## 2. Tests

- fwtest suites with golden files: boot to the tick; tick period and jitter within a stated tolerance over at least one emulated second; the heartbeat driven by the tick; a deliberate fault and an unexpected interrupt each detected and reported; the idle wait actually used (instructions per period should fall sharply against M0; record by how much).
- Read docs/HARNESS.md's rules on waiting and capture timing before writing timing tests, and design the tests so their timing is exact.
- R-BOOT-*/R-IRQ-*/R-CLK-* requirements in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, traced in the record.

## 3. Performance and budgets

- The perf gate compares against the latest main record, so the expected drop in instructions per period shows as an improvement. Code size will grow: if it exceeds the M0 budgets, move to M1 budgets in their own small PR first (What/Why/How/Result), with headroom you justify.
- Startup now uses the stack before the fill runs (if it does): move the fill earlier or measure startup separately, and say which in the design notes.

## 4. Records and notes

- DESIGN-NOTES.md entries for each choice (clock settings, vector table layout, handler conventions, tick period, idle), citing HW IDs, SDK files or your experiments; PROVENANCE.md for every source used.
- Small commits and PRs with the What/Why/How/Result/Sources/Exposure template.

## Done when

- The firmware boots to a periodic tick with the heartbeat on it and idles between ticks; faults and stray interrupts are caught.
- All suites pass deterministically in CI; the record is PASS with traceability; the audit passes; budgets hold.
- PLAN.md records M1's results and says M2 (screen) is next.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Don't archive your own transcript.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py)
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src defines=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --define)
                case "$2" in
                    ''|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) echo "build: --define takes a NAME of A-Z, 0-9 and _" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                defines="$defines $2"; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e SB_DEFINES="$defines" \

1	<!--
2	SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
3	SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
4	-->
5	
6	# fwtest: the harness, as a black box
7	
8	`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
9	emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
10	memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
11	It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
12	its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
13	Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
14	belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.
15	
16	fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
17	authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.
18	
19	## Running it
20	
21	The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
22	published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
23	(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.
24	
25	```sh
26	tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
27	tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
28	tools/fwtest version
29	tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
30	```
31	
32	- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
33	  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
34	  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
35	  be empty or not exist yet.
36	- The container has no network and runs as your user.
37	- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
38	  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
39	  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
40	  its environment.
41	
42	## The raw image
43	
44	| Rule | Value |
45	|------|-------|
46	| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
47	| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
48	| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
49	| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
50	| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
51	| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
52	| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
53	| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
54	| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
55	| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |
56	
57	## Time
58	
59	- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
60	  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
61	- Everything happens at exact emulated times, and the outputs are
62	  deterministic (below), but **while core 0 waits, fwtest moves time ahead**,
63	  so that waiting costs (almost) no instructions and instruction counts
64	  measure work. The rules for that, and what they do to captures, are
65	  exact; they follow.
66	
67	### When fwtest treats core 0 as waiting
68	
69	Two things, and nothing else, count as waiting:
70	
71	1. **The wait-for-interrupt instruction**, executed by core 0 while no
72	   interrupt is pending. Time jumps to one cycle before the next scheduled
73	   event (below). With nothing scheduled, time doesn't jump.
74	2. **Polling the free-running timer**: reading its count (HW-13 in
75	   `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the 24 MHz time base), outside an interrupt handler
76	   of core 0, for the third time or more in a row with each read coming
77	   within 64 cycles (64 instructions of core 0) of the one before. On each
78	   such read, time jumps ahead by up to 20 µs, and never past one cycle
79	   before the next scheduled event. The read then returns the count for
80	   the new time.
81	   - **Only the spacing of the reads matters.** What the loop does between
82	     them doesn't: stores to RAM, arithmetic, reads of other registers, a
83	     call. A loop that reads the count every few instructions *and* writes
84	     a heartbeat to RAM on every pass is waiting, by this rule.
85	   - A read more than 64 cycles after the previous one starts the count
86	     again, so a loop whose reads are at least 64 instructions apart is
87	     never treated as waiting.
88	   - Reads made while core 0 is in an interrupt handler are ignored: they
89	     neither count, nor jump, nor break a sequence.
90	   - Reads by core 1 count in the same sequence as core 0's: the rule
91	     looks at reads of the count, not at which core made them.
92	   - Other timers' counters, their pending flags, and RAM flags are not
93	     part of this rule. Polling them never moves time ahead.
94	
95	**Scheduled events** are what the emulated chip and the script have coming
96	next:
97	- the end of a timer period;
98	- an audio half-buffer finishing;
99	- a transfer completing;
100	- a MIDI byte arriving;
101	- an encoder contact changing;
102	- a script event.
103	
104	They count whether or not their interrupt is enabled. **Captures, the end
105	of the run and the watchdog are not scheduled events:** a jump never stops
106	for them.
107	
108	### What that does to captures
109	
110	- fwtest looks at the board between runs of core 0 instructions. Each run
111	  is at most 1024 instructions, and no longer than the instructions that
112	  would reach the next capture (or the end of the run) at one cycle each.
113	  Captures, the watchdog, halts and the end of the run are checked only
114	  between runs. A capture is taken at the first such stop at or after its
115	  time.
116	- **While core 0 is busy (not waiting), captures are exact:** taken at the
117	  first instruction boundary at or after the time asked.
118	- **While core 0 waits, a capture can come late**, because every jump
119	  inside a run moves time without using up the run's instructions:
120	  - Polling the timer: each read can add up to 20 µs. A loop that reads the
121	    count every *k* instructions can move up to about 1024 / *k* × 20 µs in
122	    one run, for example 2 ms when *k* is 10. A capture asked for at *t*
123	    can be taken that much after *t*.
124	  - Wait-for-interrupt: each wait jumps to the next scheduled event. A run
125	    that wakes on every event can cross many of them, for example several
126	    milliseconds of 100 µs interrupts.
127	- What is late is the moment the capture is taken, not its label. RAM and
128	  screen captures show the state at the moment fwtest took them, but are
129	  named for the time asked (`ram-…-10ms.bin`). `leds.csv`'s `ms` column is
130	  the time asked, while each duty value covers the real time since the
131	  previous sample. The end of the run, and so every `end` capture, can come
132	  late in the same way. `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run
133	  really ended.
134	- The watchdog compares its word between runs, so a hang is noticed up to
135	  one run late.
136	- None of this varies between runs: the same image, script and options give
137	  the same late times, byte for byte, everywhere.
138	
139	### Getting exact timing
140	
141	- **Don't wait around the times you capture.** Keep core 0 busy then, for
142	  example by spacing reads of the timer's count at least 64 instructions
143	  apart, or by waiting on something else: another timer's pending flag, or
144	  a RAM flag that an interrupt handler sets. Captures are then exact.
145	- **Or let the image record the time itself.** Store the timer's count (or
146	  your own tick count) next to what you capture, and check the capture
147	  against that stored time instead of the time asked. The M0d firmware's
148	  beacon does this (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md).
149	- **For the end of a run**, read `emulated_ms` in `result.json`.
150	- Instruction counts (`instructions` in `result.json`, `ipb.csv`) do not
151	  include the time jumped over: a waiting image's counts stay small and
152	  stable.
153	
154	## The command line
155	
156	```
157	fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
158	fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
159	fwtest version
160	```
161	
162	`run` options:
163	
164	| Option | What it does |
165	|--------|--------------|
166	| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
167	| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
168	| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
169	| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
170	| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
171	| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
172	| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
173	| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
174	| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
175	| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
176	| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
177	| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
178	| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
179	| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |
180	
181	WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
182	earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.
183	
184	## Input scripts
185	
186	A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
187	milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
188	the order written.
189	
190	```
191	# time   event
192	2        key 12 down
193	4        key 12 up
194	6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
195	10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
196	12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
197	15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
198	20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
199	```
200	
201	| Event | Meaning |
202	|-------|---------|
203	| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
204	| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
205	| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
206	| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
207	| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |
208	
209	Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
210	to the panel and to the key matrix.
211	
212	## Outputs
213	
214	All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
215	`result.json` and `junit.xml`.
216	
217	| File | Contents |
218	|------|----------|
219	| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
220	| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
221	| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
222	| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
223	| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
224	| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
225	| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
226	| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
227	| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |
228	
229	`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
230	`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
231	`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
232	`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
233	(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.
234	
235	- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
236	  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
237	- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
238	  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
239	  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
240	  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.
241	
242	## Outcomes and exit codes
243	
244	| Exit | Outcome | When |
245	|------|---------|------|
246	| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
247	| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
248	| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
249	| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
250	| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
251	| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |
252	
253	When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
254	and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
255	means fwtest itself failed.
256	
257	## Golden files
258	
259	`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
260	of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
261	without a golden file are not compared.
262	
263	- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
264	  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
265	- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
266	  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
267	  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
268	    within N.
269	  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
270	  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
271	    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
272	    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
273	    will use.
274	- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
275	  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
276	  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.
277	
278	## Suites
279	
280	`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:
281	
282	```
283	# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
284	boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
285	stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
286	```
287	
288	NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
289	EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
290	case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
291	also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
292	per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
293	on a usage error.
294	
295	## Determinism
296	
297	The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
298	on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
299	seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
300	in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
301	and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
302	differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.
303	
304	## Versions
305	
306	`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
307	`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
308	harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
309	digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.
310

# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times, and the outputs are
  deterministic (below), but **while core 0 waits, fwtest moves time ahead**,
  so that waiting costs (almost) no instructions and instruction counts
  measure work. The rules for that, and what they do to captures, are
  exact; they follow.

### When fwtest treats core 0 as waiting

Two things, and nothing else, count as waiting:

1. **The wait-for-interrupt instruction**, executed by core 0 while no
   interrupt is pending. Time jumps to one cycle before the next scheduled
   event (below). With nothing scheduled, time doesn't jump.
2. **Polling the free-running timer**: reading its count (HW-13 in
   `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the 24 MHz time base), outside an interrupt handler
   of core 0, for the third time or more in a row with each read coming
   within 64 cycles (64 instructions of core 0) of the one before. On each
   such read, time jumps ahead by up to 20 µs, and never past one cycle
   before the next scheduled event. The read then returns the count for
   the new time.
   - **Only the spacing of the reads matters.** What the loop does between
     them doesn't: stores to RAM, arithmetic, reads of other registers, a
     call. A loop that reads the count every few instructions *and* writes
     a heartbeat to RAM on every pass is waiting, by this rule.
   - A read more than 64 cycles after the previous one starts the count
     again, so a loop whose reads are at least 64 instructions apart is
     never treated as waiting.
   - Reads made while core 0 is in an interrupt handler are ignored: they
     neither count, nor jump, nor break a sequence.
   - Reads by core 1 count in the same sequence as core 0's: the rule
     looks at reads of the count, not at which core made them.
   - Other timers' counters, their pending flags, and RAM flags are not
     part of this rule. Polling them never moves time ahead.

next:
- the end of a timer period;
- an audio half-buffer finishing;
- a transfer completing;
- a MIDI byte arriving;
- an encoder contact changing;
- a script event.

of the run and the watchdog are not scheduled events:** a jump never stops
for them.

### What that does to captures

- fwtest looks at the board between runs of core 0 instructions. Each run
  is at most 1024 instructions, and no longer than the instructions that
  would reach the next capture (or the end of the run) at one cycle each.
  Captures, the watchdog, halts and the end of the run are checked only
  between runs. A capture is taken at the first such stop at or after its
  time.
- **While core 0 is busy (not waiting), captures are exact:** taken at the
  first instruction boundary at or after the time asked.
- **While core 0 waits, a capture can come late**, because every jump
  inside a run moves time without using up the run's instructions:

    count every *k* instructions can move up to about 1024 / *k* × 20 µs in

    can be taken that much after *t*.

    that wakes on every event can cross many of them, for example several
    milliseconds of 100 µs interrupts.
- What is late is the moment the capture is taken, not its label. RAM and
  screen captures show the state at the moment fwtest took them, but are
  named for the time asked (`ram-…-10ms.bin`). `leds.csv`'s `ms` column is
  the time asked, while each duty value covers the real time since the
  previous sample. The end of the run, and so every `end` capture, can come
  late in the same way. `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run
  really ended.
- The watchdog compares its word between runs, so a hang is noticed up to
  one run late.
- None of this varies between runs: the same image, script and options give
  the same late times, byte for byte, everywhere.

### Getting exact timing

- **Don't wait around the times you capture.** Keep core 0 busy then, for
  example by spacing reads of the timer's count at least 64 instructions
  apart, or by waiting on something else: another timer's pending flag, or
  a RAM flag that an interrupt handler sets. Captures are then exact.
- **Or let the image record the time itself.** Store the timer's count (or
  your own tick count) next to what you capture, and check the capture
  against that stored time instead of the time asked. The M0d firmware's
  beacon does this (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md).
- **For the end of a run**, read `emulated_ms` in `result.json`.
- Instruction counts (`instructions` in `result.json`, `ipb.csv`) do not
  include the time jumped over: a waiting image's counts stay small and
  stable.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |

| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |

| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |

| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). | `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

324	  interrupt function attribute returns correctly. A running handler can be
325	  interrupted by a pending source of higher priority only after it has
326	  stored `reti` to its stack, and only until it loads `reti` back; sources
327	  of the same or lower priority wait until it returns. When several enabled
328	  sources are pending, the one with the highest priority is taken; between
329	  equal priorities the order is not specified. fwtest models only core 0's
330	  tick timer and software-interrupt words (HW-17, HW-23), and one vector
331	  table for both cores. Whether the chip behaves the same way is Q-10.
332	- Sources: the emulator model; E-3 and E-9 show only that handlers written
333	  with the toolchain's interrupt attribute run repeatedly and return.
334	- Standing: emulator-only

388	### HW-27: The panel
389	- Fact: The display is a 240 × 240 pixel colour TFT driven by a Sitronix
390	  ST7789-family controller, on SPI1. This spec assumes the ST7789V's
391	  command set and timing (DS). Pixels are 16-bit: 5 bits red, 6 green, 5
392	  blue.

405	### HW-29: Sending bytes to the LCD
406	- Fact: Writing a byte to `JL_SPI1->BUF` sends it to the panel. Writing a
407	  count to `JL_SPI1->CNT` sends that many bytes by DMA from the address in
408	  `JL_SPI1->ADR`. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 when a transfer is done; setting
409	  `CON` bit 13 makes a finished transfer raise interrupt source 16; writing
410	  `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. In fwtest a transfer finishes at once,
411	  the DMA may read RAM or the code window, and no other set-up of SPI1 is
412	  needed. On the chip SPI1 also needs its clock (`BAUD`), mode and pins
413	  set up (Q-6).

415	  clear, bit 13 interrupt enable; bytes and DMA bursts); SDK `hwi.h`

417	  480 bytes a row, and squares sent byte by byte, all drawn.

422	- Fact: The panel's data/command line is PC8, bit 8 of `JL_PORTC->OUT`
423	  (`0x00050080`): low while a command byte is sent, high for its parameters
424	  and for pixel data. In fwtest the line's level when each byte (or each
425	  DMA transfer) starts decides how it is taken, and the pin needs no
426	  set-up. FM-1-RE also sees bit 7 (PC7) toggled with it, probably the

435	- Fact: fwtest's panel acts on: column address set `0x2A` and row address

452	### HW-32: The panel controller's own requirements
453	- Fact: On the chip, the controller needs: 5 ms after a software reset
454	  before the next command, and 120 ms after a software reset sent in sleep
455	  mode before sleep out; 5 ms after sleep out (`0x11`) before the next
456	  command, and 120 ms before a sleep in; the pixel format set to 16 bits
457	  (`0x3A` with `0x55`) to write 16-bit pixels; sleep out and display on
458	  (`0x29`) before anything shows. fwtest needs none of these delays, and
459	  doesn't check them: on the chip a firmware that skips them may show
460	  nothing.
461	- Sources: DS pages 163 (`SWRESET`), 184 (`SLPOUT`), 196 (`DISPON`), 224
462	  (`COLMOD`).

602	- Fact: `JL_ALNK0` is at `0x00012E00`: `CON0` +0, `CON1` +4, `CON2` +8,

611	- Fact: In fwtest the output plays from a buffer in RAM at the address in
612	  `JL_ALNK0->ADR3`: two halves, one after the other, each of `LEN` 32-bit
613	  words. Words alternate left, right, left, right (`LEN` / 2 stereo frames
614	  a half). Write each sample as a 24-bit signed value in the word's low
615	  bits, sign-extended: fwtest's WAV takes the whole word shifted right

617	  uses is Q-9.

619	  `0x007FFFFF`, `0xFF800000`, `0x01000000` and `0x00000080` came out as

621	  out as the values; HARNESS ("audio.wav").

626	- Fact: In fwtest, writing `JL_ALNK0->CON0` with bit 11 set starts the

656	### HW-47: The flash chip, in fwtest
657	- Fact: In fwtest the flash chip is a 1 MiB SPI NOR chip on SPI0
658	  (`JL_SPI0`, `0x00011C00`: `CON` +0, `BUF` +8). Its chip select is PD0,
659	  bit 0 of `JL_PORTD->OUT` (`0x000500C0`), low to select; each command is
660	  sent while selected and ends when PD0 goes high. A write to `BUF` sends
661	  one byte; with `CON` bit 12 set the byte received lands in `BUF`. `CON`
662	  bit 15 reads 1 when a byte is done; writing bit 14 clears it. The chip
663	  answers JEDEC ID `0x85 0x60 0x14` and understands the common SPI NOR
664	  commands read `0x03`, fast read `0x0B`, status `0x05`/`0x35`, write
665	  enable/disable `0x06`/`0x04`, 4 KiB erase `0x20`, 64 KiB erase `0xD8`,
666	  page program `0x02` (committed when PD0 goes high). Erase and program
667	  finish at once and the status never reports busy. Changes show through
668	  the code window (HW-5). Preliminary: M7 should confirm the chip and its
669	  timing through a spec request (a datasheet for the part).
670	- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 548-557, 272 (`JL_SPI0`, `JL_PORTD`); RE
671	  `docs/io/09-storage.md` §1 (the flash is on SPI0; `CON` bits 15 and 14);
672	  HARNESS ("The flash chip", "Past the image"); the emulator model (JEDEC

723	  image can release core 1 as HW-9 says.
724	- **Q-12. MIDI input.** UART1 and the MIDI jack are not covered here (M6
725	  will ask).
